# Billing System Migration — Rollout Plan
**Scope:** Migrate 40,000 existing users from the legacy billing system ("Old") to the new billing system ("New"). Both systems run concurrently (dual-run) for the duration of the rollout.

---

## Guiding Principles

- Old billing system remains fully operational, untouched, and authoritative-fallback for any user not yet cut over.
- No irreversible action against Old (deletion, disabling, decommissioning, or removal of write access) occurs until at least one full billing cycle after 100% of users are confirmed successfully migrated and validated on New — and never within the same phase as the final migration batch.
- Every phase requires an explicit sign-off against its entry criterion before it begins; no phase auto-starts on a timer alone.
- Rollback to Old must remain possible for any migrated cohort throughout the rollout.

---

## Phase Overview

| Phase | Name | % of Users | Approx. User Count |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Canary | 1% | ~400 |
| 2 | Early Adopter Expansion | 15% | ~6,000 |
| 3 | Majority Rollout | 50% | ~20,000 |
| 4 | Full Cutover (Remaining) | 34% | ~13,600 |

(Four named phases total — satisfies "at least three.")

---

### Phase 1 — Canary (1%, ~400 users)

**Entry criterion:** New billing system has passed a full end-to-end dry run against a shadow/mirrored copy of production data with 0 reconciliation discrepancies over a 7-day shadow-run window, and rollback tooling has been tested successfully in staging.

**Cohort selection:** Internal test accounts and opted-in low-risk users (no active disputes, no enterprise/custom contracts, month-to-month plans only).

**Actions:**
- Migrate account, payment method tokens, and subscription state to New.
- Run both systems in parallel for this cohort for 3 full billing cycles; Old remains authoritative fallback.
- Daily manual reconciliation of invoices, charges, and balances between Old and New for this cohort.

**Exit criterion (to advance to Phase 2):** Zero critical billing discrepancies for 3 consecutive billing cycles; all halt-metric thresholds (see below) stayed green for the full phase duration.

---

### Phase 2 — Early Adopter Expansion (15%, ~6,000 users)

**Entry criterion:** Phase 1 exit criterion met AND a documented rollback of at least one Phase 1 user was executed successfully as a live-fire drill (not just staging).

**Cohort selection:** Broaden to standard self-serve plans across varied geographies/currencies and payment methods (cards, ACH, wallets) to surface edge cases; still exclude enterprise/custom-contract accounts.

**Actions:**
- Automate reconciliation checks (replace fully manual checks from Phase 1 with automated diffing, human review of flagged exceptions only).
- Enable customer support playbooks and staff training for New-specific billing questions.
- Run parallel billing for 2 full billing cycles.

**Exit criterion (to advance to Phase 3):** Automated reconciliation mismatch rate stays below 0.1% of transactions for 2 consecutive billing cycles; support ticket volume attributable to migration stays within 1.5x of pre-migration baseline.

---

### Phase 3 — Majority Rollout (50%, ~20,000 users)

**Entry criterion:** Phase 2 exit criterion met AND on-call/support capacity confirmed scaled to handle this cohort size AND finance sign-off on reconciliation accuracy to date.

**Cohort selection:** All remaining standard accounts, including higher-value accounts, but still excluding enterprise/custom-contract accounts, which move in Phase 4 with extra manual review.

**Actions:**
- Migrate in sub-batches of ~5,000/week rather than all at once, with reconciliation checkpoints between sub-batches.
- Continue parallel run for 1 full billing cycle per sub-batch before the next sub-batch begins.
- Old system remains fully live and authoritative fallback throughout — no decommissioning steps of any kind occur in this phase.

**Exit criterion (to advance to Phase 4):** All sub-batches clear reconciliation with mismatch rate < 0.1%; no unresolved Sev-1/Sev-2 billing incidents open.

---

### Phase 4 — Full Cutover / Remaining Users (34%, ~13,600 users)

**Entry criterion:** Phase 3 exit criterion met AND enterprise/custom-contract accounts have had a dedicated manual contract-mapping review completed (since these carry non-standard pricing logic).

**Cohort selection:** All remaining users, including enterprise/custom-contract accounts, migrated last due to complexity.

**Actions:**
- Final batch migration, again in sub-batches for the largest/most complex accounts.
- Parallel run continues for at least 1 full billing cycle post-migration for this batch, same as prior phases.
- **Old system is NOT touched for deletion/disabling/decommissioning during this phase or in the batch that completes the final migration.** Decommissioning of Old is explicitly deferred to a separate, subsequent "Phase 5 — Legacy Decommission" (out of scope for this migration rollout plan, gated on a minimum of one additional full billing cycle of 100%-on-New validation plus a formal data-retention/compliance sign-off).

**Exit criterion (rollout complete):** 100% of users successfully migrated and reconciled for 1 full billing cycle with mismatch rate < 0.1% and no open Sev-1 incidents.

---

## Halt / Rollback Metrics (numeric thresholds)

The rollout is automatically **halted** (no further users migrated into the next batch/phase, and active investigation begins) if any of the following occur at any point:

- **Billing discrepancy rate > 0.5%** of transactions in any 24-hour window (reconciliation mismatch between Old and New for migrated users).
- **Failed payment/charge rate on New increases by more than 20% relative to the pre-migration baseline** for the same cohort, measured over a rolling 24-hour window.
- **Customer-reported billing incidents exceed 10 in any single 24-hour period** for the currently-migrating cohort.
- **Reconciliation job failure or data-sync lag between Old and New exceeds 15 minutes** for more than 3 consecutive sync cycles.

Any single breach triggers an automatic halt and a rollback decision review within 1 hour; migration does not resume until root cause is identified and a fix or mitigation is verified.

---

## Risks

RISK: Payment method tokens fail to migrate or map incorrectly between old and new payment processor vaults, causing failed charges | Run a token-mapping validation pass in shadow mode before each phase and reconcile a 100% sample of tokens for Phase 1, statistical sampling thereafter | Payments Engineering Lead

RISK: Double-billing or double-charging customers during the dual-run period due to both systems independently triggering charges | Enforce a single source-of-truth charge-trigger flag per user (only one system is ever the "active charger" for a given user at a time) and add automated duplicate-charge detection with alerting | Billing Platform Engineering Lead

RISK: Enterprise/custom-contract pricing logic is not fully replicated in the new system, causing incorrect invoices for high-value accounts | Require manual contract-mapping review and sign-off for every enterprise account before Phase 4, plus a parallel invoice comparison for at least 2 cycles before contract accounts go live-only on New | Revenue/Finance Operations Lead

RISK: Customer support is overwhelmed by billing confusion or errors during a phase, degrading customer trust and increasing churn | Scale support staffing and train on New-specific issues ahead of each phase, and use ticket-volume threshold (1.5x baseline) as an automatic pause trigger | Customer Support Operations Lead

RISK: Rollback path for already-migrated users is untested or breaks under real load, leaving no safe way back to Old if New fails | Execute a live-fire rollback drill on real (opted-in) users at the end of Phase 1 before proceeding, and re-test rollback tooling before each subsequent phase | Site Reliability Engineering Lead

---

PHASES: 4
